taxonomic_note: POWO/WCVP and Flora of North America accept Bernardia myricifolia. Older reports outside its core southern-Texas range may involve B. incana or B. obovata, so the learner retains those comparison cautions.
look_here_first: Look for a shrub with small crenate leaves that are densely gray-white beneath from stellate hairs. Then confirm dioecious flowers and the 3-lobed capsule; stipule and stamen characters help separate close Bernardia species.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Deep Review B locked Travis and Uvalde from herbarium records and Medina from a botanical survey.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: The PASS uses exact county records; do not extend range from generalized Edwards Plateau habitat.

best_field_traits: broadly elliptic to orbiculate leaves with revolute crenate margins
abaxial leaf surface grayish-white and densely stellate-pubescent
caducous green-to-straw stipules lacking dark resinous exudate
3-carpellate pistil with three styles densely penicillate adaxially
morphology_keys.comparison_training: B. incana has persistent darkened resinous stipule bases and fewer stamens; B. obovata is greener and more sparsely stellate beneath with a 2-carpellate pistil. Do not identify Bernardia from stellate hairs alone because Croton can look similar.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Dense gray-white abaxial pubescence plus caducous non-resinous stipules, higher stamen count, and a 3-carpellate pistil are the strongest combination.
